title: Alma Pudding
summary: Public-domain recipe from The English and Australian Cookery Book.

preparation.description: Beat half a pound of butter to a cream
Strew in by degrees half a pound of powdered sugar and mix both together
Dredge in half a pound of flour and add a quarter of a pound of currants
Moisten with four eggs well beaten
When all the ingredients are well stirred and mixed, butter a mould that will hold the mixture
Tie it down with a cloth and put the pudding into boiling water
Boil for a couple of hours
When turned out, put on it some powdered sugar and serve

title: Berry Cake
summary: Public-domain recipe from Canadian Farm Cook Book.

preparation.description: Mix 2 eggs, 1/2 cup sugar, 1/4 cup butter, 1 cup raspberries, 1 teaspoon soda, and 1 1/2 cups flour
Bake in layers

title: Karty (Cards)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Národní domácí kuchařka česko-americká.

preparation.description: Rub two tablespoons butter until it froths
Add one whole egg, two egg yolks, two ounces fine sugar and half teaspoon vanilla

title: Galletas Ligeras (Light Cookies)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Novísimo manual del cocinero práctico chileno.

preparation.description: Combine flour, butter, sugar, and milk, and knead well
Roll out, cut into rounds, and bake in the oven

title: Caramelo (Homemade Caramel)
summary: Public-domain recipe from El Practicón: tratado completo de cocina.

preparation.description: Place half a pound of powdered sugar in a pastry pan.
Melt it by stirring with a wooden spoon.
When the sugar is well melted, let it boil over the fire for one hour at a very slow boil with the spoon inside so you can stir from time to time.
When the melted sugar has acquired a very dark brown color, add one liter of cold water.
Let the sugar, which should have solidified when the cold water was added, dissolve well over a slow fire, and let it boil for twenty minutes at the edge of the fire.
Let it cool, put it in a bottle, which should be carefully corked for use when needed.
The caramel should be the color of dark mahogany, which is obtained by making it over a slow fire.

title: Chiqueadores (Sponge Fingers)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Consejos prácticos sobre cocina, pastelería y repostería al estilo del país.

preparation.description: Beat the egg yolks with the sugar for a quarter hour
Beat the egg whites until stiff peaks form
Mix everything together
Add the flour, well sifted, being careful to only mix it
Immediately make the chiqueadores

title: Bizcochos Pinos (Pine Biscuits)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Diccionario de cocina, ó El nuevo cocinero mexicano.

preparation.description: Mix all ingredients well
Form the biscuits
Toast in the oven

title: Chocolate (Chocolate)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Cozinheiro Nacional.

preparation.description: Grate half a pound of chocolate
Place it in a vessel
Add twelve cups of water
Place over fire and let it boil until it thickens
Stir with a proper chocolate whisk
Serve

title: Marmelade de Cerises (Cherry Jam)
summary: Public-domain recipe from La Cuisinière bourgeoise.

preparation.description: Cook two pounds of sugar in the same manner as for raspberry jam. Then add four pounds of cherries after removing their pits and stems. Stir them with the sugar and let them boil together until the syrup sticks to your fingers. Remove from the fire to put in pots.

title: Appelsin-age (Orange Cake)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Skandinavisk illustreret kogebog.

preparation.description: Whip 3 egg whites and 5 egg yolks separately
Stir the yolks with 2 cups sugar and half a cup butter, add half a cup cold water and 2.5 cups flour with 2 teaspoons baking powder, then fold in the whipped egg whites

title: Almond Frosting
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Manila Cook Book.

preparation.description: Blanch almonds, pound them in a mortar with a little sugar, till a fine paste.
Beat eggs and fine white sugar to stiff icing, then add almond paste, mixing thoroughly.
Cover cake with thick coating of this and afterward with plain icing.

title: Apfelkompott (Stewed Apples)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Volks-Kochbuch.

preparation.description: Peel the apples cleanly and remove the cores.
Stew them soft and clear in the sugar water, arrange them, cook the juice down a bit more and pour it over the apples.

title: Amandelmelk (Almond Milk)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Kookboek van de Amsterdamse Huishoudschool.

preparation.description: Treat the almonds as in recipe 947. Pound the ground almonds well for 10 minutes in the stone mortar. Then mix the mass, while stirring with the pestle, with the water. If necessary, sieve the mass through a rinsed linen cloth.

title: Apple Jelly Cake
summary: Public-domain recipe from The International Jewish Cook Book.

preparation.description: Rub one cup of butter and two cups of sugar to a cream
add four eggs, whites beaten separately
add one cup of milk
add two teaspoons of baking-powder and three and one-half cups of flour
Bake in layer tins

title: Babka Czekoladowa (Chocolate Babka)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Kuchnia polsko-amerykańska.

preparation.description: Boil together one cup of brown sugar, one cup of grated chocolate, and one cup of milk, then cool
Separately, beat one cup of sugar with half cup of butter, add two eggs, half cup of sweet milk, one teaspoon of soda, two cups of flour, and one teaspoon of vanilla extract
Mix, then add the cooled milk with sugar and chocolate, mix everything again
Fill the form and bake

title: Ash Cake
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Picayune's Creole Cook Book.

preparation.description: Make the dough as for Corn Dodgers.
Shape the pone of bread like the Corn Dodgers.
Sweep a clean place on the hearth and draw out a pile of hot ashes.
Place the pone of bread on top of the ashes.
Cover with hot ashes and let bake to a nice brown.
Draw the cake out of the ashes and wipe clean with a cloth till every particle of ashes that adhered in the crevices disappeared.
Serve hot with butter or molasses.
Alternatively, wrap the cake in a layer of fig leaves before baking.

title: Barnaleves rántott borsóval (Brown Broth with Fried Peas)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Képes budapesti szakácskönyv.

preparation.description: Beat 3 eggs into 4 tablespoons of flour in a pot.

title: Almond Cake
summary: Public-domain recipe from Suomalais-amerikalainen keittokirja.

preparation.description: Peel almonds and grind finely
Beat yolks of eggs and sugar to a froth
Mix with cream, butter, flour, baking powder and almonds
Add whites of eggs, whipped to a froth
Pour the mixture in a buttered mold or in small forms and bake in a moderate oven

title: Apelsinmarmelad I (Orange Marmalade I)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Hemmets kokbok.

preparation.description: Dry the oranges and lemon well with a damp cloth and peel them.
Carefully remove all the white from the peel.
Cut the peel into fine strips and the fruit flesh into thin slices, removing all seeds.
Place everything in the cold water and let it stand 24 hours.
Place it on the fire and let it cook 1 hour.
Then add the sugar, and let the marmalade cook an additional 1 hour, or until it is clear and fairly thick.
Skim it carefully during cooking.
When most of the heat has passed, pour it into warm glass jars.

title: Butter Crust for Boiled Puddings
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Book of Household Management.

preparation.description: With a knife, work the flour to a smooth paste with 1/2 pint of water
Roll the crust out rather thin
Place the butter over it in small pieces
Dredge lightly over it some flour
Fold the paste over
Repeat the rolling once more, and the crust will be ready for use

title: Biskuittorte (Sponge Cake)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Neues Wiener Menu- und Kochbuch.

preparation.description: Beat 6 egg yolks with 12½ dkg sugar for 20 minutes
Fold in 6 stiff egg whites together with 12½ dkg flour
Fill the mixture into the form
Bake slowly
The cake can be cut through 1-2 times and filled in various ways
Fill with jam, ice white or sprinkle lightly with sugar

title: Baking Powder Biscuit II
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book.

preparation.description: Mix and bake as Baking Powder Biscuit I.

title: Caramel
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Art of Living in Australia.

preparation.description: Put half a pound of sugar into a frying-pan and let it get very brown
Pour over half a pint of water and stir till it boils
Strain into a bottle
It will keep good a long time, and is very useful for colouring soup and gravies

title: Black Pudding
summary: Public-domain recipe from Canadian Farm Cook Book.

preparation.description: Steam for 2 hours

title: Knedlíky Americké (American Dumplings)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Národní domácí kuchařka česko-americká.

preparation.description: Beat 3 eggs well
Add 1 cup sweet milk and 1 tablespoon salt to it
Mix 1 teaspoon baking powder into 3 cups flour and add to the milk
Work this well on a plate
Shape five dumplings, roll them on a rolling pin to round them, and put them in water to boil

title: Huevos Hilados (Threaded Eggs)
summary: Public-domain recipe from El Practicón: tratado completo de cocina.

preparation.description: Clarify two pounds of sugar in one liter of water, taking care that the point is weak, as soon as it begins to thread.
Sift two dozen yolks through a clear sieve with the aid of a spatula, and add them gradually to the clarified sugar, stirring very quickly during cooking, which will last two minutes.

This mass or paste is poured into a funnel of cylindrical form, whose bottom is like that of a metal strainer, with holes the size the egg threads should have, and these are collected in very cold water, aiding their passage through the funnel with a wooden pestle or handle that weighs and presses the mass.

title: Helados de Leche (Milk Ice Cream)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Consejos prácticos sobre cocina, pastelería y repostería al estilo del país.

preparation.description: Bring one liter of milk to a boil with half an ounce of cinnamon and twelve ounces of sugar
When it has boiled, remove from heat and let cool
Strain and put in the ice cream maker to set like the previous recipe
If desired, serve with a tablespoon of cinnamon snow on top

title: Hojuelas de Mantequilla y Manteca (Wafers with Butter and Lard)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Diccionario de cocina, ó El nuevo cocinero mexicano.

preparation.description: Knead the flour with warm water
As soon as it comes together, add the melted lard and butter
Work it like washing clothes
Wrap it in a napkin and remove it to stretch with lard, not hot, but at a good temperature
Drain the wafers well

title: Panada Côr de Leite (Milk-Colored Panada)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Cozinheiro Nacional.

preparation.description: Make as milk panada, but instead of fat, add a cup of milk and a tablespoon of sugar

title: Marmelade de Framboises (Raspberry Jam)
summary: Public-domain recipe from La Cuisinière bourgeoise.

preparation.description: Cook one pound of sugar in the same manner as for strawberries. When it reaches the proper cooking point, add the raspberries prepared as follows: peel two pounds of raspberries and pass them through a sieve to make jam. Put this jam on the fire to dry it until it is nearly sticking to the pan. Then put it in the sugar and let it boil a few times while stirring constantly, and then put it in your pots.

title: Boston Mais-Brod (Boston Corn Bread)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Skandinavisk illustreret kogebog.

preparation.description: Mix 1 cup sweet milk with 2 cups sour milk.
Add 2/3 cup molasses, 1 cup wheat flour, 4 cups cornmeal, and 2 teaspoons soda.
Bake for 3 hours.

title: Apple Johnny Cake
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Manila Cook Book.

preparation.description: Sift together dry ingredients, add butter and milk, and apples cut finely; stir well and bake quickly.

title: Apfelmus (Apple Puree)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Volks-Kochbuch.

preparation.description: Peel the apples and cut them into pieces.
Cook them quickly with the water in a heated pot until soft, press the cooked apples through a sieve and mix the puree with the sugar.

title: Amandelnootjes (Almond Cookies)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Kookboek van de Amsterdamse Huishoudschool.

preparation.description: Wash the unpeeled almonds, dry them and grind them fine.
Mix them with the stiffly beaten egg white, the sifted flour and the sugar and shape this dough into small rolls about 1 cm thick.
Lay these on a greased baking sheet and bake them in a moderately warm oven until light brown and done (15-20 minutes). Remove them from the baking sheet and let them cool.

title: Bell Fritters
summary: Public-domain recipe from The International Jewish Cook Book.

preparation.description: Stir three eggs until very light
Stir in one cup of sweet milk
Sift in three cups sifted flour
Beat for ten minutes
Add three teaspoons of baking-powder
Fry by spoonfuls in hot oil
Serve with any sweet sauce

title: Babka Śnieżna (Snow Babka)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Kuchnia polsko-amerykańska.

preparation.description: Beat eleven egg whites into foam, add one teaspoon of cream of tartar and beat further until the foam is stiff
Slowly add one and a half cups of sugar, one cup of flour sifted with quarter teaspoon of salt and mix
Add one teaspoon of vanilla extract, place in a form and put in the oven for forty-five to fifty minutes
After baking, turn the form onto a plate and let the babka fall out by itself

title: Baked Batter Pudding
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Creole Cookery Book.

preparation.description: Beat eggs separately and very light
Stir flour in gradually while the milk is boiling hot
Bake 1/2 hour in a quick oven
Serve with wine and sugar sauce
This pudding must be sent to the table as soon as it is done

title: Appelsiinimarmelaadia (Orange Marmalade)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Keittokirja = Cook Book.

preparation.description: Wipe carefully oranges and lemons.
Peel and remove the white part of the peel.
Cut the peel in strips, simmer in 1½ cups water for ½ hour.
Divide the fruit sections, remove the seeds and the fibre.
Let simmer in 1½ quarts water for ½ hour.
Drain without stirring through a fine cheese cloth.
Cook stirring constantly the drained liquor with sugar and the cooked yellow rind in its liquor for 15 minutes.
Fill the glass jars, cover as directed.
Serve with tea and toast.

title: Apelsinmarmelad I (Orange Marmalade I)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Hemmets kokbok.

preparation.description: Wipe the oranges and lemon well with a damp cloth and peel them.
Carefully remove all the white from the peel.
Cut the peel into fine strips and the fruit flesh into thin slices, removing all pits.
Place everything in the cold water and allow it to stand for 24 hours.
Place it on the stove and allow it to cook for 1 hour.
Then add the sugar, and allow the marmalade to cook for a further 1 hour, or until it is clear and fairly thick.
During cooking skim it carefully.
When most of the heat has dissipated, pour it into warm glass jars.

title: Common Short Crust
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Book of Household Management.

preparation.description: Crumble the butter into the flour as finely as possible
Add the sugar
Work the whole up to a smooth paste with the boiling milk
Roll it out thin
Bake in a moderate oven

title: Brandteig (Choux Pastry)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Wiener Kochbuch.

preparation.description: Put 1/4 liter of milk and 5 Deca of butter in a saucepan and bring to a boil.
Stir in 22 Deca of flour and stir this dough over the fire until it is dry and separates from the spoon and saucepan.
Transfer the dough to a deep bowl and let it cool with occasional stirring.
Once cooled, stir in 5 whole eggs, which causes the dough to stretch and take on a yellow color.
Neither sugar nor salt should be added during the preparation of this dough.
Use for various purposes.

title: Batter III
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book.

preparation.description: Mix and sift dry ingredients, add milk gradually, and egg well beaten.

title: Derby Cakes
summary: Public-domain recipe from The English and Australian Cookery Book.

preparation.description: Rub half a pound of butter into a pound of flour
Put in half a pound of currants, half a pound of sugar, and one egg
Mix all together with a quarter of a pint of milk
Cut them into round cakes
Bake

title: Breakfast Puffs
summary: Public-domain recipe from Canadian Farm Cook Book.

preparation.description: mix the liquid and add the flour gradually
beat until light
pour into hot buttered gems
Bake 30 to 35 minutes in hot oven

title: Čokoládová omáčka (Chocolate Sauce)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Česká kuchařka.

preparation.description: Boil everything together
Stir slowly until it thickens
Allow to cool

title: Marquesote de Harina (Flour Sponge Cake)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Consejos prácticos sobre cocina, pastelería y repostería al estilo del país.

preparation.description: Beat sixteen egg whites to stiff peaks
Have one pound of flour and one pound of ground sugar sifted
Once the egg whites are well beaten, add the sugar and the egg yolks and finally the flour, mixing without beating
Place in greased molds and put in a gentle oven

title: Mamones de Harina de Trigo (Wheat Flour Sponge Cakes)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Diccionario de cocina, ó El nuevo cocinero mexicano.

preparation.description: Beat twelve egg whites and sixteen egg yolks until the mixture is white and thick
Add one pound of flour little by little so that it does not become lumpy
Shape the mamones into long shapes like ladyfingers or round
To make a crust, beat eighteen eggs and pour over them with ground sugar
Put in the oven until they toast slightly

title: Marmelade de Framboises (Raspberry Marmalade)
summary: Public-domain recipe from La Cuisinière bourgeoise.

preparation.description: Cook a pound of sugar the same way as for strawberries
When it is at its cooking point, add the raspberries prepared as follows: clean two pounds of raspberries and pass them through a sieve to make marmalade
Put this marmalade on the fire to dry it until it is ready to stick to the pan

title: Cherries with Vinegar
summary: Public-domain recipe from Frøken Jensens kogebog.

preparation.description: The sugar can be chosen between powdered sugar, icing sugar or Demerara sugar, the latter gives the best juice.
Place the sugar in the pot in layers with the pitted berries, and pour the vinegar over.
The pot should initially be placed over low heat, while stirring occasionally.
As soon as the cherries boil, skim them and remove them on a colander, but not before they begin to wrinkle; usually one counts 10 minutes of boiling.
Pour the cherries, from which the juice must have drained well, into a jar, and reduce the juice until it is fairly thick.
Pour it boiling over the cherries, which can then be sealed immediately with parchment paper.
If desired, some pieces of whole cinnamon and some cloves can be boiled with the juice.

title: Boiled Corn Bread
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Manila Cook Book.

preparation.description: Mix sweet milk, molasses, flour, corn meal and soda, dissolved in sour milk.
Pour into a greased mould (a small lard pail answers the purpose), cover and boil for two hours.

title: Butterteig zu Pasteten (Butter Pastry for Pastries)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Neuestes Süddeutsches Kochbuch.

preparation.description: Make the dough as in recipe 267
Fold this dough five times on top of each other, because it should not rise as much

title: Boterbollen (Butter Balls)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Betje de goedkoope keukenmeid.

preparation.description: Mix 2½ ounces wheat flour with ¼ quart milk and let simmer slowly with constant stirring.
When cooled slightly, slowly beat in 4 eggs.
Roll into small balls and fry in not too hot oil.

title: Browning for Soups
summary: Public-domain recipe from An Easy and Economical Book of Jewish Cookery.

preparation.description: Put into a small yellow basin 1/4 lb. sugar
Put it into your oven and let it get almost like hardbake, a deep brown colour
While it is bubbling up pour over it half a pint of boiling water off the fire
Let it stand, then stir it well
Strain it through a sieve
When quite cold bottle it for use

title: Bułeczki Kukurydzane - Drugi Przepis (Corn Rolls - Second Recipe)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Kuchnia polsko-amerykańska.

preparation.description: Mix 1 cup cornmeal and 0.5 cup wheat flour and add 1.5 teaspoons baking powder and sift together to mix well.
Beat 1 egg, add 1.5 cups sweet milk and mix all into dough.
Place in forms and bake in a hot oven.

title: Boiled Custard
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Picayune's Creole Cook Book.

preparation.description: Set the milk to boil.
Beat the yolks of the eggs and the sugar very light.
Beat the whites to a stiff froth, and stir carefully into the yolks and the sugar.
Moisten the cornstarch with a little cold milk, and stir into the boiling milk.
Continue to stir until it commences to thicken.
Then add the sugar and the eggs.
Stir and let it cook for one moment longer, and take from the fire.
Add the vanilla, and turn into a dish to cool.
Serve very cold.

title: Apple Marmalade
summary: Public-domain recipe from Suomalais-amerikalainen keittokirja.

preparation.description: Wash apples, cut in pieces and cook in 3 cupfuls of water until it becomes a sauce.
Force through a sieve and return to the fire.
Simmer with sugar stirring all the time until of firm consistency.
Spread on an oiled or buttered platter.
Cut in pieces, dip in granulated sugar and dry.

title: Apelsinmarmelad III (Orange Marmalade III)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Hemmets kokbok.

preparation.description: Dry the oranges and lemons well with a damp cloth and cut them in halves.
Cut each half into thin slices, and carefully remove the seeds.
Pour the cold water over the fruit, which is then allowed to stand for 12 hours.
The next day let everything cook until the peels become transparent, and then let it stand another 24 hours.
Then add the marmalade together with the sugar and let it cook under skimming until it becomes clear.
When most of the heat has passed, pour it into small glass jars.

title: Very Good Short Crust for Fruit Tarts
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Book of Household Management.

preparation.description: Rub the butter into the flour, after having ascertained that the latter is perfectly dry
Add the sugar, and mix the whole into a stiff paste, with about 1/3 pint of water
Roll it out two or three times, folding the paste over each time, and it will be ready for use

title: Choux Pastry (Éclair-Bäckerei)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Wiener Kochbuch.

preparation.description: Place butter, sugar, and flour in saucepan
Pour boiling water over and stir constantly
Boil until dough releases from spoon
Set aside and let cool completely
Gradually stir in egg yolks one by one
Place dough on flour-dusted board
Form into desired shapes such as breads, rods, rings
Place on butter-lined baking sheet
Brush with water
Sprinkle with hail sugar
Bake at low heat in oven until pale golden

title: Batter IV
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book.

preparation.description: Mix and sift dry ingredients, add milk gradually, and egg well beaten.

title: Plain Pound Cake
summary: Public-domain recipe from The English and Australian Cookery Book.

preparation.description: Beat separately
Bake in the same way as the twelfth cake, with less time

title: Brown Jelly Cake
summary: Public-domain recipe from Canadian Farm Cook Book.

preparation.description: Mix all ingredients
Bake

title: Čokoládová Zmrzlina (Chocolate Ice Cream)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Česká kuchařka.

preparation.description: Place three-quarters liter milk, quarter liter cream and six ounces grated chocolate in a pan
Heat and constantly stir
Let it cool
Proceed as with other ice creams

title: Marquesote (Spanish Sponge Cake)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Consejos prácticos sobre cocina, pastelería y repostería al estilo del país.

preparation.description: Beat the egg whites until stiff peaks form
When they are well set, mix in the egg yolks and the sugar, ground and sifted
Then add the sifted flour
Put in small greased molds and place in the oven

title: Masa para Cubrir un Pastel (Dough to Cover a Pastry)
summary: Public-domain recipe from La cocinera poblana.

preparation.description: Knead 1 pound of flour with 4 whole eggs, 4 ounces of lard, and 5 ounces of sugar with all fingers without adding water
Extend with a rolling pin on a board, leaving it slightly thicker than a peso coin
Butter the inside of a cooking pot and cover it well with this dough
Fill according to directions given elsewhere
Cover with another layer of the same dough after filling

title: Pâte à Biscuit (Biscuit Dough)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Le Cuisinier impérial.

preparation.description: Break 15 eggs, putting the whites in one bowl and the yolks in another
With the yolks use 1 pound of powdered sugar

title: Citron Sauce (Lemon Sauce)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Skandinavisk illustreret kogebog.

preparation.description: Press out the Juice from a Lemon and grate the Shell.
Put 1 Ounce Butter over the Fire and mix it with 1 Ounce Sugar until it boils.
Then stir in 1/4 Pint boiling Water, 1 Ounce Sugar, Lemon Shell and Juice.
The Sauce is served for Puddings.
It must not boil after the Lemon is added, as it will otherwise become bitter.

title: Burnt Leather Cake
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Manila Cook Book.

preparation.description: Burn syrup: One-half cup sugar stirred in a pan until it burns
Add one half cup boiling water and boil until thick syrup
Cream butter and sugar
Add the yolks of eggs well beaten, water and two cups of flour, sifted three times
Beat for five minutes
Then add three teaspoons of burnt syrup, baking powder stirred into one half cup of flour, whites of eggs well beaten

title: Citroneneis (Lemon Icing)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Neuestes Süddeutsches Kochbuch.

preparation.description: Rub the zest of one lemon on one quarter pound sugar
Finely pound and sieve the remaining sugar
Press the juice of the lemon into it
Beat one egg white to snow
Stir it together for a quarter hour and use as desired

title: Witbrood (White Bread)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Kookboek van de Amsterdamse Huishoudschool.

preparation.description: Put the flour in a deep bowl, make a well in the middle, crumble the yeast into it and mix with about half of the lukewarm milk.
Stir in enough of the surrounding flour to form a thick dough (so-called starter).
Let this rise covered on a lukewarm spot for 20 to 30 minutes.
Then add the remaining milk and salt and knead this dough until it leaves the hands.
Let it rise covered on a lukewarm spot (about 1 hour).
Shape it so that a greased bread pan is filled about 2/3.
Let the dough rise here for another 1/2 hour and bake the bread in a hot oven, placed approximately in the middle, brown and done (1/2 to 3/4 hour).
Brush the top as soon as it becomes brown with water to get a shiny crust.
Tap on the bread to hear if it is done and turn it out of the pan.
Note: Replace the milk with water if desired.

title: Cup Cake
summary: Public-domain recipe from The International Jewish Cook Book.

preparation.description: Cream one cup of butter with two cups of sugar
Add gradually the yolks of four eggs, one at a time
Sift three cups of flour, measure again after sifting, and add two teaspoons of baking-powder in the last sifting
Add alternately the sifted flour and one cup of sweet milk
Add last the beaten whites of the eggs
Flavor to taste
Bake in loaf or jelly-tins

title: Farsz Czekoladowy (Chocolate Filling)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Kuchnia polsko-amerykańska.

preparation.description: Cook together for five minutes: quarter pound of chocolate, one cup of sugar, three-quarters cup of water and two tablespoons of butter
Mix two tablespoons of cornstarch in quarter cup of milk, pour into the chocolate mixture and cook another three minutes
Beat with a spoon until it cools, then add one teaspoon of vanilla extract

title: Brown Roux
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Picayune's Creole Cook Book.

preparation.description: Melt the tablespoonful of butter slowly
Add gradually the flour, sprinkling it in and stirring constantly, till every portion is a nice, delicate brown
Never make it too brown, because it must continue browning as the other ingredients are added

title: Black Cake
summary: Public-domain recipe from Suomalais-amerikalainen keittokirja.

preparation.description: Beat molasses, add butter, beaten eggs, cream, ginger, soda and flour.
Bake in a hot oven.

title: Berlinerbröd (Berlin Bread)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Iduns kokbok.

preparation.description: Dry the almonds in a cloth and chop fairly coarsely.
Wash the butter and stir for 10 minutes, thereafter add the sugar, the eggs one at a time, the almonds and the sifted flour, well mixed with the baking powder.
Place the dough with 2 spoons on a well buttered baking sheet in approximately 2 1/2 cm. wide strips, which are baked a nice golden brown in a not too hot oven.
Cut the strips at once diagonally into 1 cm. wide breads, which are dried well in a warming oven.

title: Crème au Caramel (Caramel Cream)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Wiener Kochbuch.

preparation.description: Put 12 deca crushed sugar in a saucepan and let it brown
Gradually pour 1/4 liter cold water onto it
Let it boil well and then cool
Meanwhile, beat 1/2 liter cream with 4 egg yolks and 6 deca sugar
Put this in a snow kettle
Add the cooled caramel sugar
Beat over heat until the mass begins to thicken
Use immediately

title: Belle's Muffins
summary: Public-domain recipe from Common Sense in the Household.

preparation.description: Sift the cream tartar with the flour
Beat the eggs very light
Dissolve the soda in hot water
Bake in rings in a quick oven

title: Butter Tarts
summary: Public-domain recipe from Canadian Farm Cook Book.

preparation.description: Beat eggs
Mix with brown sugar, butter, currants and vanilla
Fill tart shells
Bake

title: Tenké koláčky (Thin Cookies)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Česká kuchařka.

preparation.description: Mix butter, flour, sugar, eggs, and sour cream to form dough
Knead the dough well and roll it out
Cut cookies with a small form or glass
Bake on waxed sheet and sprinkle with sugar

title: Panque (Cake)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Consejos prácticos sobre cocina, pastelería y repostería al estilo del país.

preparation.description: Work together very well 0.5 pound of sugar with 0.5 pound of butter and 12 egg yolks
After half an hour of beating, add the 12 well-beaten egg whites
Place in a mold greased with butter and bake in the oven

title: Orejas (Ears)
summary: Public-domain recipe from La cocinera poblana.

preparation.description: Knead so that it incorporates
Extend with a rolling pin
Cut the shapes with a mold
Send to the oven

title: Esser (Letter S Cakes)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Illustreret kogebog for by og land.

preparation.description: Mix wheat flour, butter, powdered sugar, and eggs together
Form into small tea cakes shaped like an S using a pastry bag
Bake brown at strong heat

title: Butter Scotch
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Manila Cook Book.

preparation.description: Boil all together until it hardens when dropped into cold water.
Spread thinly on buttered pans and mark in little squares.

title: Eier in Sole (Pickled Eggs)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Volks-Kochbuch.

preparation.description: Cook the eggs in boiling water with the salt for 10 minutes
Crack the tips of the eggshells
Place the eggs in cooled salt water where they will keep for a long time
After 2-3 days they can be used
Optional: place the pickled eggs in cooled ham or curing brine for 1 to 3 days in winter

title: Currants
summary: Public-domain recipe from The International Jewish Cook Book.

preparation.description: Treat the same as raspberries.

title: Kluski Pulchne (Fluffy Dumplings)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Kuchnia polsko-amerykańska.

preparation.description: Bring half a cup of butter and one cup of water to a boil in a pot and slowly add one cup of flour to the boiling liquid, stirring at the same time so a uniform mass forms.
Remove from heat and cool well, then add two eggs and mix properly.

From this dough dumplings can be made in three ways: 1) Take with a spoon and place dumplings on simmering soup, then cover so they rise; 2) make small round balls with fingers and fry them in hot fat, of which there must be much in the pot; 3) fill a buttered baking tin with dough to half full, place in a pot with hot water and cook in steam, cool, cut with a knife into cubes and place in a bowl before filling it with soup.

title: Burnt Sugar
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Picayune's Creole Cook Book.

preparation.description: Take one pound of granulated sugar, and set it on the fire, and stir with a wooden spoon until thoroughly dissolved and burnt black
Add one quart of water, and let it boil until thoroughly dissolved
Reduce to half the quantity and strain and bottle for use

title: Buttermilk Cake
summary: Public-domain recipe from Suomalais-amerikalainen keittokirja.

preparation.description: Mix all the dry ingredients with butter in a bowl
Turn the batter on a floured board
Knead diligently
Divide the dough into two parts
Roll into cakes 1/3 inch thick
Flour them
Cut the cakes into six equal parts
Fry them or bake in oven about 10-15 minutes
When frying on the stove the cakes have to be turned over so as to be evenly done on both sides
Do not make the batter hard
Serve hot

title: Biskvéer (Macarons)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Iduns kokbok.

preparation.description: Blanch the almonds, dry them in the oven and pass through an almond mill.
Stir the egg whites and sugar for 1/2 hour, whereupon add the almonds and stir the mass for another 10 minutes.
Place the dough with a teaspoon in small dollops on a well cleaned, buttered and floured baking sheet.
Bake the macarons in weak oven heat until they are light yellow and release from the sheet.

title: Creme im Dunst mit Chocolate (Steamed Cream Pudding with Chocolate)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Wiener Kochbuch.

preparation.description: It is prepared in the same way as the 'Creme im Dunst mit Vanille' (No. 1426). One softens 16 deca chocolate on a baking sheet in a warm oven, then puts it into a saucepan, stirs it thoroughly smooth with 1/2 liter boiling water over the fire and mixes it into the already prepared cream without vanilla.

title: Boiled Indian Meal Pudding
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Virginia Housewife; Or, Methodical Cook.

preparation.description: Mix one quart of corn meal, with three quarts of milk; take care it be not lumpy
add three eggs and a gill of molasses
put it on at sun rise, to eat at three o'clock
tie the bag properly, as the meal swells very much

title: Butter Tarts
summary: Public-domain recipe from Canadian Farm Cook Book.

preparation.description: Cream sugar and butter together
Add eggs and currants
Bake in medium hot oven in tart shells

title: Zmrzlina Citrónová se Smetanou (Lemon Ice Cream with Cream)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Česká kuchařka.

preparation.description: Grate one lemon into 330 grams sugar
Place four eggs, half liter cream and the sugar on a warm stove
Constantly whip while heating
Remove from heat, let cool and constantly whip
Place in ice cream machines

title: Pastel Serafín (Serafín Cake)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Consejos prácticos sobre cocina, pastelería y repostería al estilo del país.

preparation.description: Place powdered sugar, eggs, and vanilla in a copper pot
Place over gentle heat or double boiler
Beat the contents of the pot until it reaches a foamy appearance and has doubled in volume
Add sifted flour carefully, adding melted butter
Pour this batter into a mold buttered and dusted with flour
Put in a hot oven to bake quickly
Pour some of the batter into small fluted molds, similarly buttered and floured
Place on a bed of ash and put in the oven
When baked, place the cake on a platter with the small molds around it

title: Pastel de Mata Fina (Fine Dough Cake)
summary: Public-domain recipe from La cocinera poblana.

preparation.description: Take two pounds of flour
Add fourteen egg yolks and one pound of butter, adding the butter a little at a time, with half a pound of ground sugar
Knead everything, and the consistency of the dough should be like a pearl
Extend a little dough on the plate as if making tortillas and then wrap the rest of the dough around it
Before doing so, separate a little of the same dough and make long strips with which to form around the wrapper some braids that serve as decoration

title: Gode Raad (Good Advice Cakes)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Skandinavisk illustreret kogebog.

preparation.description: Mix 1 pound flour, ½ pound butter, 4 eggs, and ½ pound powdered sugar together into a stiff dough
Place a small piece in the center of the iron and bake
Grease the iron for each cake
This makes 24 cakes

title: Caramel Custard
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Manila Cook Book.

preparation.description: Beat eggs thoroughly
Add four tablespoons of sugar, milk, and vanilla
Make custard
Make a caramel of four tablespoons sugar browned
Have ready little tin moulds and put in each one teaspoon of hot caramel
Turn quickly in your fingers so as to coat the sides of the mould with caramel as evenly as possible
Fill the moulds about three-fourths full of the custard
Place them in a pan of hot water
Bake in the oven until the custard is set
Turn out of the moulds while warm and serve cold

title: Sandtorte (Sand Torte)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Neuestes Süddeutsches Kochbuch.

preparation.description: Melt 1/2 pound butter in a bowl
Stir in 6 egg yolks, 1/2 pound fine sugar, the grated zest of 1 lemon, the beaten whites from 6 eggs, and 1/2 pound flour very thick with the butter
Fill the mixture into a mold and bake the torte in the oven

title: Glace for Candies
summary: Public-domain recipe from The International Jewish Cook Book.

preparation.description: Boil one pound of sugar with one-half pint of water until it ropes
Add one-half cup of vinegar and boil until it hardens
Dip in fruit, orange slices, nuts or green grapes with stems on
Put aside on a buttered platter to set

title: Lukier Gotowany (Cooked Icing)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Kuchnia polsko-amerykańska.

preparation.description: Cook sugar, water, and cream of tartar over low heat until a small amount of the mixture dropped in cold water forms a soft ball
Beat one egg well
Pour the sugar mixture into the egg in the thinnest stream possible, stirring constantly
Spread on cake with a knife dipped in warm water
Chopped almonds or nuts may be added to this icing

title: Buttermilk Cake
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Picayune's Creole Cook Book.

preparation.description: Beat the butter to a cream, and then add the sugar, which has been sifted fine.
Beat to a cream.
Add the yolks of the eggs, and continue beating till very light.
Mash the soda in the buttermilk, dissolving thoroughly, first in a half cupful, and then mixing well with the remainder of the milk.
Add this to the eggs and butter.
Then gradually add the sifted flour, and beat till very smooth.
Lastly add the whites of the eggs, beaten to a stiff froth.
Bake for forty-five minutes in a moderate oven.

title: Caramel Ice Cream
summary: Public-domain recipe from Suomalais-amerikalainen keittokirja.

preparation.description: Brown 1 cupful of granulated sugar in a pan.
Mix with ½ cupful of water stirring until the sugar is dissolved.
Take care not to burn the sugar only let it get delicate brown.
Use this caramel instead of vanilla and sugar in vanilla ice cream base.

title: Biskvier (Almond Biscuits)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Iduns kokbok.

preparation.description: Blanch the almonds, dry them in the oven and drive through an almond mill.
Whip the egg whites and sugar for 1/2 hour, then add the almonds and stir the mass for another 10 minutes.
Place the dough with a teaspoon in small clumps on a well-cleaned, buttered and floured baking sheet.
Bake the biscuits in weak oven heat until they are light yellow and release from the baking sheet.

title: Erdbeer-Gefrornees mit Kern und Obersgefrornees (Strawberry Frozen Dessert with Core and Cream Frozen Dessert)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Wiener Kochbuch.

preparation.description: Stir 20 deca sugar with 8 egg yolks well together in a snow-beater

title: Boiled Rice
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book.

preparation.description: Pick over rice; add slowly to boiling, salted water, so as not to check boiling of water.
Boil thirty minutes, or until soft, which may be determined by testing kernels.
Old rice absorbs much more water than new rice, and takes longer for cooking.
Drain in coarse strainer, and pour over one quart hot water; return to kettle in which it was cooked; cover, place on back of range, and let stand to dry off, when kernels are distinct.
When stirring rice, always use a fork to avoid breaking kernels.

title: Butter Tarts
summary: Public-domain recipe from Canadian Farm Cook Book.

preparation.description: Stir well
Put in tart shells
Bake in oven

title: Polvorones (Shortbread Cookies)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Consejos prácticos sobre cocina, pastelería y repostería al estilo del país.

preparation.description: Place the sifted flour, sifted sugar, and lard on a table
Mix very well until the dough is silky
Roll out with a rolling pin
Cut into desired shapes
Place on a hot oven to cook quickly

title: Rosquitas de Leche (Milk Rings)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Diccionario de cocina, ó El nuevo cocinero mexicano.

preparation.description: Sweeten eleven quarts of milk with two and a half pounds of sugar
Strain it and put it on the fire until it reaches the point of candy
Remove it and extract through a syringe, immediately forming the rings

title: Hindbær og Ribs (Raspberry and Currant Jam, English Jam)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Frøken Jensens kogebog.

preparation.description: Remove stems from the raspberries and currants.
Layer them in the pot alternately with the sugar.
Place over low heat until the berries begin to release juice.
Skim well and boil for 3/4 hour.
Pour into jars and tie them up immediately.

title: Caramel Filling
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Manila Cook Book.

preparation.description: Boil until it starts to string from spoon.

title: Weißes Eis (White Icing)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Neuestes Süddeutsches Kochbuch.

preparation.description: Pound one quarter pound sugar very finely
Pass it through a hair sieve
Beat one egg white into it and add the juice of one lemon
Stir for a quarter hour until it is completely white and use as desired

title: Grafton Cake
summary: Public-domain recipe from The International Jewish Cook Book.

preparation.description: Cream four tablespoons of butter with one and one-half cups of sugar
Beat in separately two whole eggs
Add one cup of milk alternately with two cups of flour in which has been sifted two teaspoons of baking-powder
Beat all thoroughly
This recipe will make two layer cakes which may be spread with any of the cake fillings or icings
To make small cakes omit one of the egg-whites, fill well-buttered gem pans a little more than half full, and bake in a moderately hot oven until a delicate brown
The white reserved may be beaten to a stiff froth and then gradually stir in four tablespoons of powdered sugar and the juice of half a lemon
When the cakes are cool, spread with the icing and decorate with raisins, nut meats, one on top of each or sprinkle with candied caraway seeds

title: Lukier Twardy (Hard Icing)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Kuchnia polsko-amerykańska.

preparation.description: Beat the powdered sugar, lemon juice, and boiling water strongly until a smooth, half-transparent mass forms
Cover the cake while hot, immediately after removing from the oven

title: Caramel
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Picayune's Creole Cook Book.

preparation.description: Continue boiling till the sugar reaches a light brown color
Take the vessel off immediately, or it will burn
On taking the vessel from the fire, insert the bottom in cold water to prevent the sugar from burning

title: Corn Cake (Maissi kakku)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Suomalais-amerikalainen keittokirja.

preparation.description: Mix flour and corn meal with salt and baking powder.
Whip eggs with sugar, add milk and melted butter to it.
Mix with flour, stirring thoroughly together.
Bake in a shallow pan in hot oven.

title: Brynt smör (Brown Butter)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Iduns kokbok.

preparation.description: Brown the butter until it takes on a beautiful light brown color, but do not let it burn.
Add the parsley and pour the butter at once over the dish with which it is to be served, or serve it in a sauce bowl.

title: Geschnittenes Wurm (Cut Worm Noodles)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Wiener Kochbuch.

preparation.description: Make firm dough from 2 whole eggs, 1 egg yolk, and 1/3 liter flour
Work and knead dough
Cut very finely with a sharp knife
Rub several times with flat hands
Push through a sieve

title: Boston Cream Cakes
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook.

preparation.description: Put into a large-sized saucepan half a cup of butter and one cup of hot water.
Set it on the fire; when the mixture begins to boil, turn in a pint of sifted flour at once.
Beat and work it well with a vegetable masher until it is very smooth.
Remove from the fire.
When cool enough add five eggs that have been well beaten, first the yolks and then the whites, also half a teaspoonful of soda and a teaspoonful of salt.
Drop on buttered tins in large spoonfuls about two inches apart.
Bake in a quick oven about fifteen minutes.
When done and quite cold, open them on the side with a knife or scissors and put in as much of the custard as possible.
For cream filling: Put two-thirds of a pint of milk over the fire in a double boiler.
In a third of a pint of milk, stir two eggs, three tablespoonfuls of sifted flour (or half cup of cornstarch) and one cup of sugar.
As soon as the milk looks like boiling, pour in the mixture and stir briskly for three minutes, until it thickens.
Remove from the fire and add a teaspoonful of butter.
When cool, flavor with vanilla or lemon and fill your cakes.

title: Canned Raspberries
summary: Public-domain recipe from Canadian Farm Cook Book.

preparation.description: To every 3 pounds sugar allow 1 quart water, and boil for 1/4 hour
Draw kettle to back of stove, where mixture will not boil
Let it remain till you have jars filled with fruit
After jars are filled stand on a wet cloth and fill with the hot syrup
Seal and put a sack or cloth in a tub
Put jars in and pour boiling water in until jars are covered
Let stand until cool

title: Royal (Baking Powder)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Consejos prácticos sobre cocina, pastelería y repostería al estilo del país.

preparation.description: Mix all ingredients very well in dry form.
Store in a covered jar.
Use in the same way as commercial baking powder.

title: Soletas Mas Consistentes de Harina Sola (Firmer Soletas with Flour Alone)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Diccionario de cocina, ó El nuevo cocinero mexicano.

preparation.description: Make following all the procedures of the previous soletas articles, using twenty eggs, twelve ounces of sugar, and one pound of flour

title: Hindbær (Raspberry Preserve)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Frøken Jensens kogebog.

preparation.description: Boil the sugar and water together.
Add the berries and bring to a boil.
Drain the berries through a sieve.
Boil the drained juice until it is smooth.
Pour the berries back into the juice and bring to a boil again.
Pour into glasses and tie them up as soon as the preserve has cooled.

title: Cheese Straws
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Manila Cook Book.

preparation.description: Mix cheese, butter and flour together, moisten with a little cold water.
Roll thin, cut into strips and bake in medium oven.

title: Raspberries and Currants
summary: Public-domain recipe from The International Jewish Cook Book.

preparation.description: Heat, crush and press the juice from the currants and proceed as directed for raspberries.

title: Maliny Konserwowane (Preserved Raspberries)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Kuchnia polsko-amerykańska.

preparation.description: Fill jars with berries and arrange in a large steamer
Cook on steam for half an hour
Make a syrup from sugar and water and cook it for five minutes
Uncover the steamer and immediately pour the syrup over the berries
Jars should be full

title: Cherry Compote
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Picayune's Creole Cook Book.

preparation.description: Put the sugar and water into a saucepan, and when it makes a syrup add the cherries
Let them boil up

title: Custard Filling
summary: Public-domain recipe from Keittokirja = Cook Book.

preparation.description: Add to 1 cup boiling milk 1 tablespoon cornstarch mixed with 4 tablespoons sugar
Boil up
Flavor with vanilla and thicken with 2 egg yolks
Reheat, not allowing it to boil
Let cool
May be flavored with lemon, orange or any fruit juice preferred, dissolved chocolate, chopped almonds, or black coffee

title: Brynt smör (Browned Butter)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Iduns kokbok.

preparation.description: Brown the butter until it has a beautiful light brown color, but do not let it burn.
Add the parsley and pour the butter immediately over the dish with which it is to be served, or serve it in a sauce bowl.

title: Marmelade von Himbeeren (Raspberry Marmalade)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Allgemeines österreichisches oder neuestes Wiener Kochbuch.

preparation.description: Pass 8 pounds of well-selected raspberries through a fine sieve
Place the sieved berries in a casserole over a charcoal fire
Stir constantly until reduced to half
Clarify and cook 4 pounds of sugar as described above
Add the berry mass to the sugar
Proceed as for cherry marmalade

title: Boston Favorite Cake
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book.

preparation.description: Cream the butter, add sugar gradually, eggs beaten until light, then milk and flour mixed and sifted with baking powder.
This recipe makes two loaves, or one-half the mixture may be baked in individual tins.

title: Caramel Custard
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Canadian Family Cook Book.

preparation.description: Put sugar in pan
Stir until it melts and is light brown
Add the water
Stir into the warm milk
Beat eggs lightly
Add salt and vanilla and part of the milk
Strain into the remainder of the milk
Pour into a buttered two-quart mould
Set the mould in a pan of warm water
Bake from thirty to forty minutes, or till firm
Serve with cream and fruit sugar

title: Torta de Almendra y Huevo sobre Hojas de Masa (Almond and Egg Cake on Pastry Sheets)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Diccionario de cocina, ó El nuevo cocinero mexicano.

preparation.description: Grind twelve ounces of almonds with half a pound of butter
When removed from heat, stud with toasted almonds and prick all over with the point of a knife
Fill these cuts with very thick syrup and dust with ground sugar and cinnamon

title: Jelsy Cake (Jelly Cake)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Skandinavisk illustreret kogebog.

preparation.description: Stir 1.5 cups sugar with half a cup butter, half a cup sweet milk
Whip 3 eggs separately and stir the whites in last
Sift 2.5 cups flour and 2 teaspoons baking powder into the mixture
Bake in pie or jelly pans in the usual way
For the filling: cook together 1 cup sugar, 1 egg, grated lemon zest, 1 tablespoon water, and 1 teaspoon flour, then cool and place in thick layers between the cakes as usual

title: Common Batter
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Manila Cook Book.

preparation.description: Mix in very smooth batter, a little thicker than batter cakes

title: Wheat Muffins
summary: Public-domain recipe from The International Jewish Cook Book.

preparation.description: Mix two cups of flour, one-half teaspoon of salt, three teaspoons of baking-powder, two tablespoons of sugar
Sift these ingredients twice
Rub in one tablespoon of butter
Separate one egg
Beat the yolk and add it to one cup of milk and one teaspoon of molasses
Mix with the dry ingredients
Stir until smooth
Fold in the beaten white of egg
Pour into hot, well-greased muffin-tins
Bake fifteen to twenty minutes in hot oven

title: Tort Zwyczajny (Standard Layer Cake)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Kuchnia polsko-amerykańska.

preparation.description: Cream half cup of butter with one cup of sugar
Add half cup of milk and half teaspoon of salt
Add two egg yolks
Mix in two cups of flour with two teaspoons of baking powder sifted together
Mix well and then add the egg whites beaten to foam, mixing only lightly
Divide the batter in half and bake in a moderately hot oven on two plates
After removing from the oven, spread some filling on one layer, place the other layer on top, and frost the entire cake

title: Cherry Pie
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Picayune's Creole Cook Book.

preparation.description: Stew the cherries gently, as for a marmalade
Prepare the pie crust according to directions, and proceed as in directions for making pies

title: Dumplings
summary: Public-domain recipe from Suomalais-amerikalainen keittokirja.

preparation.description: Mix all dry ingredients and rub butter with fingers into it.
Add milk gradually.
Roll into a sheet 1/2 inch thick.
Cut it into small circles with a round cutter.
Place into the kettle to boil on the meat so as not to break them.
Serve immediately because the dumplings will fall quickly.
Instead of butter, 1/2 cupful of chopped suet may be used, and water instead of milk.

title: Citronglace (Lemon Ice Cream)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Hemmets kokbok.

preparation.description: Dry the lemons, rub the yellow peel against the sugar, and press out the juice.
Mix the water, lemon juice and sugar well, then strain.
Mix in the egg white, and pour everything into an ice cream machine to freeze.

title: Nußkrapferl (Nut Pastry)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Neues Wiener Menu- und Kochbuch.

preparation.description: Knead the flour, sugar, butter and egg yolk on the board to a dough
After resting, roll out
Cut into rounds
Place on an unbuttered baking sheet
Bake at higher heat until light brown
Join 2 pieces together with filling
Top with ½ nut or sprinkle with sugar unglazed

title: Butter Scotch
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book.

preparation.description: Boil ingredients together until, when tried in cold water, mixture will become brittle.
Turn into a well buttered pan; when slightly cool, mark with a sharp-pointed knife in squares.
This candy is much improved by cooking a small piece of vanilla bean with other ingredients.

title: Caramel Icing (Variation)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Canadian Farm Cook Book.

preparation.description: Boil until thick enough to spread on the cake

title: Torta de Arroz (Rice Cake)
summary: Public-domain recipe from La cocinera poblana.

preparation.description: Grind the rice and sugar together
Melt the butter
In a bowl mix the rice, sugar, melted butter, egg yolks and one unbeaten egg white
Beat well
Once at the proper consistency, fold in seven beaten egg whites, beaten as for nougat (turrón)
Beat a little more
Grease a mold with butter
Pour all into it and place over two fires or bake in the oven

title: Jordbær-Gelé (Strawberry Jelly)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Frøken Jensens kogebog.

preparation.description: Pick over the strawberries and treat them just like raspberries No. 98.
Used like the preceding varieties for Russian marmalade.

title: Corn Bread
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Manila Cook Book.

preparation.description: Mix and sift dry ingredients.
Add milk, eggs well beaten, and butter.
Bake in shallow buttered pan in hot oven twenty minutes.

title: Cherry Sherbet
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Picayune's Creole Cook Book.

preparation.description: Boil the sugar and water together for five minutes
Stone the cherries and add them to the syrup
Set to cool
Press through a sieve till all the juice is extracted from the cherries
Set to freeze and serve as directed

title: Finnish Sponge Cake
summary: Public-domain recipe from Suomalais-amerikalainen keittokirja.

preparation.description: Beat yolks of eggs and sugar to a thick froth
Add flour slowly into it
Lastly mix with stiffly beaten whites of eggs
Bake in a buttered mold in a moderate oven nearly 3/4-1 hour
Garnish, when cold, with white icing

title: Citronglace (Lemon Ice Cream for 6 persons)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Hemmets kokbok.

preparation.description: Dry the lemons, rub the yellow peel against the sugar, and squeeze out the juice.
Mix the water, lemon juice and sugar well, then strain it.
Mix in the egg white and pour everything into an ice cream machine to freeze.

title: Salzsticks von Wasserteig zum Tee (Salted Sticks of Water Dough for Tea)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Wiener Kochbuch.

preparation.description: Place water and butter in a saucepan and bring to a boil
While stirring constantly, add flour gradually and stir over the fire until the dough is dry and pulls away from the spoon and pan
Spread the dough on a flour-dusted board and let cool covered
Roll the dough knife-back-thick, cut out with desired cutters, and place on a buttered baking sheet
Make light cuts with a knife, brush with beaten egg, sprinkle with finely crushed salt
Bake until golden in the oven
Remove from sheet with a knife and serve with tea

title: Cambridge Gingerbread
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book.

preparation.description: Melt butter in water, add molasses, egg well beaten, and dry ingredients mixed and sifted.
Bake in a buttered shallow pan.

title: Children's Cake
summary: Public-domain recipe from Canadian Farm Cook Book.

preparation.description: Mix butter, sugar, and milk
Add flour and baking powder
Add vanilla and eggs
Bake in layer cake or sponge cake form

title: Torta de Mantequilla Compuesta (Composed Butter Cake)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Diccionario de cocina, ó El nuevo cocinero mexicano.

preparation.description: Beat the egg whites and egg yolks separately as you would for marquesote, and after bringing them together, beat them again

title: Maître d'Hôtel Butter
summary: Public-domain recipe from Skandinavisk illustreret kogebog.

preparation.description: Mix together 1 ounce butter, 1 tablespoon chopped parsley, 1 teaspoon lemon juice and 0.25 teaspoon pepper
Mix together cold and spread on what you wish to use it for
It is excellent for any kind of fried fish

title: Corn Muffins
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Manila Cook Book.

preparation.description: Mix together cornmeal, milk, flour, butter, eggs and sugar, and add baking powder just before baking.

title: Cherry Water
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Picayune's Creole Cook Book.

preparation.description: Stone the cherries and press the juice from the pulp into a porcelain vessel
Add a little water and the juice of one lemon
Stir well and let stand for two hours
Wash the stones well and pound them fine, and add to the cherries, and add eight ounces of sugar
