preparation.description: Flavor to taste
Drop by teaspoonfuls, and bake quickly

title: Omenamarmelaadia (Apple Marmalade)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Keittokirja = Cook Book.

preparation.description: Wash and cut the apples in pieces.
Cook with water to a sauce.
Force the apple sauce through a strainer and return to the fire.
Add the sugar and simmer stirring continuously until of firm consistency.
Spread a platter with oil or butter and pour marmalade over, spreading with a knife.
When cold, cut in squares, dip in granulated sugar and dry.

title: Smält Smör med Hackade Ägg (Melted Butter with Chopped Eggs)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Hemmets kokbok.

preparation.description: Hard boil the eggs, cut and chop them.
Clarify the butter, remove the white foam.
Place the chopped eggs in the sauce bowl and pour the clarified butter over.

title: Ginger Pudding
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book.

preparation.description: Cream the butter, add sugar gradually, and egg well beaten
Mix and sift dry ingredients
Add alternately with milk to first mixture
Turn into buttered mould
Cover and steam two hours
Serve with Vanilla Sauce

title: Hot Water Sponge Cake
summary: Public-domain recipe from Canadian Farm Cook Book.

preparation.description: Sift flour and cream tartar together
Whip sugar and egg to a cream
Add sifted flour
Add soda in hot water last
Bake in a hot oven

title: Large Thread
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Picayune's Creole Cook Book.

preparation.description: Boil the sugar a little longer
Try as before; if a thread forms that can be pulled two inches without breaking, this degree is reached

title: Orange Marmelade
summary: Public-domain recipe from Suomalais-amerikalainen keittokirja.

preparation.description: Wipe oranges and lemons carefully.
Peel and remove the white part from inside of peels.
Slice yellow rinds and put to simmer for 1/2 hour with 1 1/2 cupfuls of water.
Cut the fruit in pieces, remove seeds.
Place in kettle to simmer for 1/2 hour with 1 1/2 cupfuls of water.
Pour on a tight cloth to drain without stirring.
Simmer the drained juice mixed with sugar, sliced and cooked rinds of fruit and their own liquor for 15 minutes stirring constantly.
Place the marmalade in small jars and preserve as directed.
Serve with tea and toast.

title: Smält Smör med Persilja (Melted Butter with Parsley)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Hemmets kokbok.

preparation.description: Rinse the parsley well and chop it.
Clarify the butter, remove the white foam, and stir in the chopped parsley.

title: Grilled Almonds
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook.

preparation.description: Blanch a cupful of almonds; dry them thoroughly
Boil a cupful of sugar and a quarter of a cupful of water till it hairs
Throw in the almonds; let them fry, as it were, in this syrup, stirring them occasionally
They will turn a faint yellow brown before the sugar changes color; do not wait an instant once this change of color begins, or they will lose flavor
Remove them from the fire, and stir them until the syrup has turned back to sugar and clings irregularly to the nuts

title: Ice Cream No. 3
summary: Public-domain recipe from Canadian Farm Cook Book.

preparation.description: Beat egg whites and yolks separately
Beat 2 cups granulated sugar with yolks
Mix all well together: beaten eggs, sugar, 1 pint cream, 1 quart milk, and 1 tablespoon vanilla
Freeze
This makes 1 gallon ice cream

title: Lemon Pastilles
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Picayune's Creole Cook Book.

preparation.description: Proceed in the same manner as for Orange Pastilles

title: Peach Short Cake
summary: Public-domain recipe from Suomalais-amerikalainen keittokirja.

preparation.description: Wash butter and work to a cream with sugar
Mix with flour and lastly with beaten eggs
Bake in two molds to light brown
Lay fruit between and on the cakes
Serve with whipped cream

title: Smält smör (Melted Butter)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Iduns kokbok.

preparation.description: Melt the butter just before serving and season, if desired, with salt and lemon juice.
If the butter is allowed to stand and clarify, it loses in flavor and becomes hard-melted.
If the butter is used for fried fish, let it cook until it has taken on a golden color and has a faint hazelnut aroma.
Then season it with lemon juice and pour it at once over the fish, which has been previously sprinkled with chopped parsley.

title: Hard Sugar Gingerbread
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book.

preparation.description: Cream the butter, add sugar gradually, milk, and dry ingredients mixed and sifted.
Put some of mixture on an inverted dripping-pan and roll as thinly as possible to cover pan.
Mark dough with a coarse grater.
Sprinkle with sugar and bake in a moderate oven.
Before removing from pan, cut in strips four and one-half inches long by one and one-half inches wide.

title: Icing for Devil Cake
summary: Public-domain recipe from Canadian Farm Cook Book.

preparation.description: cook till waxy
then add vanilla and beat till creamy
then spread between layers and on top of cake

title: Little Drop Cakes
summary: Public-domain recipe from La Cuisine Creole.

preparation.description: Combine all ingredients
Mix and bake

title: Plain Cake
summary: Public-domain recipe from Suomalais-amerikalainen keittokirja.

preparation.description: Rub butter and sugar to a cream, add well beaten eggs, milk, vanilla, baking powder mixed with flour into it.
Pour the mixture in a buttered mold and bake in a moderate oven.

title: Smörgröt (Butter Porridge)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Iduns kokbok.

preparation.description: Heat the milk. Fry the butter and flour for 2 minutes, gradually add the milk while stirring, and let the porridge cook for 15 minutes. Season with salt and serve with milk.

title: Harvard Pudding
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book.

preparation.description: Mix and sift dry ingredients and work in butter with tips of fingers
Beat egg, add milk, and combine mixtures
Turn into buttered mould
Cover and steam two hours
Serve with warm Apple Sauce and Hard Sauce

title: Jelly Cake 2
summary: Public-domain recipe from Canadian Farm Cook Book.

preparation.description: Beat eggs and sugar until light
Add the cream and soda and cream tartar sifted in the flour by taking good measure
Bake (this will make three good cakes)

title: Maizena Cake
summary: Public-domain recipe from La Cuisine Creole.

preparation.description: Rub half a pound of butter to a cream with one pound of powdered sugar
Beat six eggs lightly
Add one pound of corn starch
Flavor and bake in small patty pans

title: Plain Pastry for Pies
summary: Public-domain recipe from Suomalais-amerikalainen keittokirja.

preparation.description: Work thoroughly together flour, salt and butter
Pour gradually water into it
Knead to an even paste
Put in a cold place for a while
Roll the paste into 1/2 inch thick crust, a little larger than the pie-plate
Place the crust on the floured pie plate
Spread the edges of the crust with water or white of egg
Have the upper crust a little larger than the under crust
Perforate the upper crust so that the steam may escape
Cover the filling with the upper crust pressing the edges well together
Cut the edges to fit evenly and fold down the edges of the upper crust
Spread with egg and tie around the edges with a wet cloth, 1 inch wide
Bake until lightly browned, first in hot oven then reducing the heat, 1 hour

title: Smörkäx (Butter Cookies)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Iduns kokbok.

preparation.description: Sift the flour. Work the butter into half of the flour with fingertips, then add the milk and finally the rest of the flour except 1 kkp, which is set aside for baking.
Work the dough until it becomes even and smooth, then cover it and let it stand in a cold place for one day.
Roll out the dough thinly, prick it well and cut out with a large round mould into cookies, which are baked light yellow in a warm oven.
Serve with marmalade or butter.

title: Hot Water Gingerbread
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book.

preparation.description: Add water to molasses.
Mix and sift dry ingredients.
Combine mixtures and add butter.
Beat vigorously.
Pour into a buttered shallow pan.
Bake twenty-five minutes in a moderate oven.

title: Klondike Cake
summary: Public-domain recipe from Canadian Farm Cook Book.

preparation.description: Mix ingredients together and bake

title: Molasses Cookies
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Picayune's Creole Cook Book.

preparation.description: Melt the molasses
Beat the butter and sugar to a cream, and add, mixing in the soda, dissolved in a tablespoonful of boiling water
Add the ginger and the ground cloves
Take off the fire, and beat till cool
Then add the eggs, beaten well

title: Pop-overs
summary: Public-domain recipe from Suomalais-amerikalainen keittokirja.

preparation.description: Put all ingredients in a bowl and whip well for 5 minutes.
Pour the batter in hot, buttered, deep iron molds.
Bake for 30 minutes, first in hot oven.
When risen, reduce heat.
Do not touch them before they are quite hard.

title: Smörkäx (Butter Crackers)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Iduns kokbok.

preparation.description: Sift the flour. Work the butter into half of the flour with the fingertips, then add the milk and finally the rest of the flour.

title: Ice Cream Candy
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book.

preparation.description: Boil ingredients together without stirring, until, when tried in cold water, mixture will become brittle.
Turn on a well buttered platter to cool.
As edges cool, fold towards centre.
As soon as it can be handled, pull until white and glossy.
While pulling, flavor as desired.

title: Ladies' Fingers
summary: Public-domain recipe from Canadian Farm Cook Book.

preparation.description: Beat the butter, sugar and egg until very light
Add vanilla and milk
Add flour sifted with baking powder

title: One, Two, Three, Four Cup Cake
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Picayune's Creole Cook Book.

preparation.description: Beat the butter to a cream.
Add the sugar.
Beat till very light.
Beat the eggs (yolks and whites together) till very light, and add them gradually to the butter and sugar, beating all the while.
Beat vigorously.
Add the sifted flour, and beat thoroughly until very light.
Line a round cake pan with the buttered paper, and fill with the mixture.
Set in a moderate oven, and bake for one hour and a quarter.

title: Sally's Muffins (Sallyn muffensit)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Suomalais-amerikalainen keittokirja.

preparation.description: Sift flour with salt and baking powder.
Whip eggs with sugar, add milk and melted butter.
Pour it slowly into the flour kneading well.
Bake in greased muffin tins.
Serve with tea or as luncheon bread.

title: Ugnstekt Potatis i Skivor (Oven-Baked Sliced Potatoes)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Hemmets kokbok.

preparation.description: Peel the potatoes and cut them into slices.
Grease a baking pan with some of the butter, lay the potatoes in rows in it and sprinkle with salt and grated cheese.
Place the remaining butter in flakes on top, and put the potatoes in the oven to bake through.

title: Indian Pudding
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book.

preparation.description: Pour milk slowly on meal, cook in double boiler twenty minutes, add molasses, salt, and ginger; pour into buttered pudding-dish and bake two hours in slow oven; serve with cream. If baked too rapidly it will not whey. Ginger may be omitted.

title: Layer Cake
summary: Public-domain recipe from Canadian Farm Cook Book.

preparation.description: Cream sugar and butter
Add eggs well beaten
Add last, milk and flour sifted with the baking powder
Bake in 3 layers and put together with lemon filling or icing
Ice top and side

title: Plain Fritter Batter for Meats, Poultry, etc.
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Picayune's Creole Cook Book.

preparation.description: Beat the yolks of the eggs and the flour together, and add the melted butter and the salt.
Then add the water, and beat well, and finally add the whites of the eggs, beaten to a stiff froth.
Some add a half teaspoonful of baking powder according to taste.

title: Sallyn muffensit (Sally's Muffins)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Keittokirja = Cook Book.

preparation.description: Sift together flour, salt and baking powder
Beat the eggs with sugar, add milk and melted butter
Pour gradually the flour in, stirring well
Bake in buttered muffin tins

title: Ugnstekt Potatis i Skivor (Oven-Roasted Sliced Potatoes)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Hemmets kokbok.

preparation.description: Peel the potatoes and cut them into slices.
Grease a baking pan with some of the butter, lay the potatoes in rows in it and sprinkle with salt and grated cheese.
Place the remaining butter in flakes on top, and put the potatoes in the oven to cook through.

title: Jelly-Cake
summary: Public-domain recipe from Common Sense in the Household.

preparation.description: Bake in shallow tins, and when cold put jelly between.

title: Lemon Marmalade
summary: Public-domain recipe from Canadian Farm Cook Book.

preparation.description: Slice 12 lemons very thin, and take out the seeds
Pour over them 5 quarts of water and let them stand all night
The next morning put them on in the same water, and let them boil until tender enough to mash with a spoon
Add six pounds of sugar and boil 30 minutes
Do not cover until cold

title: Pop-Overs
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Picayune's Creole Cook Book.

preparation.description: Beat the yolks of the eggs separately till very light and frosty
Stir in the unskimmed milk and the flour that has been twice sifted with the baking powder
Add the whites of the eggs, beaten to a stiff froth
Pour the mixture into buttered cake tins
Bake in a quick oven till a light brown, and serve either hot or cold

title: Sitruunakastike No. 1 (Lemon Sauce No. 1)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Keittokirja = Cook Book.

preparation.description: Mix the sugar with the cornstarch
Add gradually the boiling water, stirring well
Cook until clear
Remove from the fire, add the lemon juice and butter

title: Vindböjtlar (Choux Pastries)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Hemmets kokbok.

preparation.description: Bring water, butter and sugar to a boil
Whisk in the flour and let the batter cook until it releases from the pan
Once most of the heat has dissipated, stir in the egg yolks one at a time; finally fold in the egg whites beaten to stiff peaks
Press the batter through a pastry bag or corrugated piping cone onto a well-cleaned and buttered baking sheet in the shape of swans or other figures
Bake in a hot oven
During baking, the oven door should be opened as infrequently as possible, as the draft will cause the pastries to collapse and become flat
If the bottom heat of the oven is too strong, use double baking sheets

title: Johnnie Cake
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook.

preparation.description: Sift one quart of Indian meal into a pan
make a hole in the middle and pour in a pint of warm water, adding one teaspoonful of salt
with a spoon mix the meal and water gradually into a soft dough
stir it very briskly for a quarter of an hour or more, till it becomes light and spongy
spread the dough smoothly and evenly on a straight, flat board (a piece of the head of a flour-barrel will serve for this purpose)
place the board nearly upright before an open fire and put an iron against the back to support it
bake it well
when done, cut it in squares
send it hot to table, split and buttered

title: Light Cake
summary: Public-domain recipe from Canadian Farm Cook Book.

preparation.description: Dissolve soda in water
Cream tartar in flour
Mix all ingredients together

title: Pound Cake
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Creole Cookery Book.

preparation.description: Cream butter
Mix the sugar
Put in flour and eggs alternately
Bake 2 hours

title: Sitruunakohokas (Lemon Souffle)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Keittokirja = Cook Book.

preparation.description: Whip the yolks with the sugar, add the yellow rind and the juice of the lemon and the bread crumbs.
Beat the egg whites until firm, add to the yolks.
Bake in a well-buttered mold for 20-30 minutes, having the mold in a pan of water.

title: Vindböjtlar (Choux Pastry Puffs)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Hemmets kokbok.

preparation.description: Bring water, butter, and sugar to a boil
Whisk in the flour, and let the mixture cook until it pulls away from the pan
Once most of the heat has dissipated, stir in the egg yolks one at a time; lastly fold in the egg whites beaten to stiff peaks
Press the mixture through a piping bag or fluted pastry cone onto a well-cleaned and buttered baking sheet in the shape of "S"s or other figures
Bake in a warm oven
During baking, open the oven door as seldom as possible, as the draft will cause the pastries to collapse and become flat
If the oven's bottom heat is too strong, use double baking sheets

title: Lemon Butter
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book.

preparation.description: Cream the butter, and add slowly lemon juice

title: Love Cake
summary: Public-domain recipe from Canadian Farm Cook Book.

preparation.description: Make base with 1 cup sugar, 3/4 cup butter, 2 eggs, 1 cup sweet milk, 3 teaspoons baking powder, and 2 1/2 cups flour
Take out for two layers
Add to third layer 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon, 3/4 teaspoon cloves, and 1 cup raisins
Put third layer between an icing

title: Preserved Tomatoes
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Creole Cookery Book.

preparation.description: Make the syrup first
Put the fruit in and let it remain a short time over a slow fire
They do not require a great deal of cooking

title: Sitruunakohokas (Lemon Souffle)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Suomalais-amerikalainen keittokirja.

preparation.description: Beat yolks and sugar to a froth.
Stir grated yellow lemon rind, juice and bread crumbs into it.
Lastly add the stiff beaten whites.
Pour the mixture in a well buttered individual mold.
Steam in oven about 20-30 minutes.
Serve hot in the mold.

title: Lemon Ice
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book.

preparation.description: Make a syrup by boiling water and sugar twenty minutes
add lemon juice
cool, strain, and freeze

title: Maple Cream Icing
summary: Public-domain recipe from Canadian Farm Cook Book.

preparation.description: Boil
Stir until cold

title: Raspberry Jam
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Picayune's Creole Cook Book.

preparation.description: Select fine, ripe fruit and weigh.
Allow equal weights of fruit and sugar.
Proceed to boil as directed.
When they begin to jelly, they are ready to be turned into glasses.

title: Small Cookies
summary: Public-domain recipe from Suomalais-amerikalainen keittokirja.

preparation.description: Wash butter and work to a cream with sugar
Add slowly eggs into it, whipping well
Lastly mix with flour
Force through a pastry bag on baking sheet cookies in shape of S
Bake about 10 minutes in a moderate oven

title: Lemon Sauce
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook.

preparation.description: Put sugar, butter, one egg beaten light, one lemon with juice and grated rind, and half a cupful of boiling water in a tin basin
Thicken over steam

title: Minster Cake
summary: Public-domain recipe from Canadian Farm Cook Book.

preparation.description: Bake 30 minutes in pan

title: Rice-Milk for Children
summary: Public-domain recipe from La Cuisine Creole.

preparation.description: Wash the rice and put it with the milk in a close-covered stewpan
set it over a slow fire
let it simmer gently for one hour and a half
It will scorch on a fierce fire

title: Sokerileipä (Sugar Cookies)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Keittokirja = Cook Book.

preparation.description: Beat until firm egg whites
Beat yolks with sugar
Add to the yolks vanilla and flour
Fold in the whites last of all
Drop by the spoonful on a buttered baking sheet
Sprinkle lightly with sugar
Bake in a slow oven until light brown

title: Lemon Sauce I
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book.

preparation.description: Make a syrup by boiling sugar and water eight minutes; remove from fire; add butter and lemon juice.

title: Mother Christie's Cookies
summary: Public-domain recipe from Canadian Farm Cook Book.

preparation.description: Use more flour if necessary to make it stiff.
Roll thin and bake in a pretty hot oven.

title: Royal Ginger Cake
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Creole Cookery Book.

preparation.description: Mix flour, sugar, and butter well together with molasses, cream, and ginger
Roll out and bake in a slack oven

title: Sokuri lankaa (Spun Sugar)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Suomalais-amerikalainen keittokirja.

preparation.description: Put 2 cupfuls of sugar in a saucepan with 1 cupful of water and 1/4 teaspoonful of cream of tartar.
Place on fire stirring until the sugar has dissolved.
Boil without stirring until the sugar gets firm when dipped in cold water, and cracks when broken.
Put the saucepan in cold water to stop boiling.
Put dipper or two forks in syrup and spin sugar from them over a stick, shaking them quickly back and forth.
Remove the spun sugar carefully from the stick and use to garnish desserts.
Keep well when covered with a bowl.

title: Lemonade
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book.

preparation.description: Make syrup by boiling sugar and water twelve minutes.
Add fruit juice, cool, and dilute with ice-water to suit individual tastes.
Lemon syrup may be bottled and kept on hand to use as needed.

title: Muffins
summary: Public-domain recipe from Canadian Farm Cook Book.

preparation.description: Mix and sift dry ingredients
Add the milk gradually and the egg well

title: Salted Almonds
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Picayune's Creole Cook Book.

preparation.description: Take about a pint of almonds and shell them
Blanch or scald them in boiling water till the skin comes off easily
Dry well and place in a flat tin dish
Add about an ounce of butter and set the plate in a moderate oven until the almonds are a golden brown
Take them out of the oven and add a heaping tablespoonful of salt
Stir them round and round, dredging quickly with the salt, and turn them into a dish to cool
Pick out the almonds and throw aside the extra salt
When cool, place in a box for use, covering tightly

title: Sokuri Lastuja (Sugar Wafers)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Suomalais-amerikalainen keittokirja.

preparation.description: Melt butter and mix with sugar.
Rub in a bowl until white.
Stir slowly eggs alternately with flour into it, whipping well.
Place a thin layer of batter on a well greased sheet and bake in a moderate oven.
Cut into pieces 3 inches long and 1 inch wide and roll them hot around a stick.
Alternatively, form the batter into round thin cookies and roll together while hot.

title: Maître d'Hôtel Butter
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book.

preparation.description: Put butter in a bowl, and with small wooden spoon work until creamy
Add salt, pepper, and parsley, then lemon juice very slowly

title: Muffins, Plain
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Canadian Family Cook Book.

preparation.description: Mix the sugar and shortening to a cream
Add the liquid
Sift the flour and baking powder into it
Beat well
Heat gem irons hot, grease, fill nearly full, and bake in hot oven twenty minutes

title: Small Thread
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Picayune's Creole Cook Book.

preparation.description: Dip the forefinger into iced water, and then into the boiling sugar, and instantly again into the iced water, to prevent burning the finger
Pinch between the index finger and thumb
If a small thread forms, which breaks when the attempt is made to pull apart through the fingers, the proper degree is reached

title: Sokuri Leipiä (Sugar Cookies)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Suomalais-amerikalainen keittokirja.

preparation.description: Beat whites of eggs to a froth.
Whip yolks with sugar until light.
Mix yolks with vanilla and flour.
Lastly stir the beaten whites into it.
Drop with spoon on greased baking sheet and sprinkle thinly with sugar.
Bake in a slow oven to a light yellow.

title: Milk Frosting
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book.

preparation.description: Put butter in saucepan; when melted, add sugar and milk. Stir, to be sure that sugar does not adhere to saucepan, heat to boiling-point, and boil without stirring thirteen minutes. Remove from fire, and beat until of right consistency to spread; then add flavoring and pour over cake, spreading evenly with back of spoon. Crease as soon as firm.

title: Mustard Cream Dressing for Cabbage
summary: Public-domain recipe from Canadian Farm Cook Book.

preparation.description: Cook in a double boiler and stir until thick
When cold, or when you want to use it, add 3 1/2 cup vinegar, and serve on chopped cabbage

title: Souffle Pudding
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Creole Cookery Book.

preparation.description: Put on your milk to boil, reserving about a gill to wet the flour
When the milk comes to a boil, add the flour which has been wet with the milk, also the butter and sugar
Let this thicken well
Put it in a bowl to get cold, at least for 1 or 2 hours before you are ready to use it
About 1/2 hour before you are ready to use, have the yolks well beaten, which you add by degrees to the cold paste
Last of all, add the whites, which have been whipped until very light
Have a yellow bowl buttered, put the paste in it, and bake in a hot oven a good 1/2 hour
Serve with a hard sauce of butter and sugar, flavored as you wish
Serve immediately, as it will fall by standing

title: Sokuri munkkia (Sugar Puffs)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Suomalais-amerikalainen keittokirja.

preparation.description: Boil up 4 cupfuls of water
Add 1/2 pound of butter into it
Reheat to boiling
Add 1/2 pound of wheat flour
Beat the mixture well until it leaves the sides of the pot

title: Naples Biscuit
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Virginia Housewife; Or, Methodical Cook.

preparation.description: Beat twelve eggs light
add to them one pound of flour, and one of powdered sugar
continue to beat all together till perfectly light
bake it in long pans, four inches wide, with divisions; so that each cake, when done, will be four inches long, and one and a half wide

title: Mustard Sauce
summary: Public-domain recipe from Canadian Farm Cook Book.

preparation.description: Mix mustard in vinegar
Add eggs, white sugar, butter, and salt
Cook in double boiler

title: Stage Planks or Ginger Bread Without Butter or Eggs
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Picayune's Creole Cook Book.

preparation.description: Melt the molasses, lard and ginger together and blend well.
When thoroughly melted and warmed, beat for about ten minutes.
Then dissolve the soda in a tablespoonful of boiling water and add to the molasses.
Mix it thoroughly, and then add the flour, using good judgment and adding just enough of the three cups of sifted flour to make a stiff batter.
Beat thoroughly and vigorously.
Have ready several greased, shallow pans; pour the mixture into them and bake for ten minutes in a quick oven.

title: Sour Milk Griddle Cakes
summary: Public-domain recipe from Suomalais-amerikalainen keittokirja.

preparation.description: Prepare and bake as griddle cakes.

title: Omelette Robespierre
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book.

preparation.description: Beat eggs slightly, and add remaining ingredients.
Put one and one-half tablespoons butter in a hot omelet pan.
Turn in mixture and cook same as French Omelet.
Fold, turn on a hot platter.
Sprinkle with powdered sugar, and score with a hot poker.

title: No. 1 Cookies
summary: Public-domain recipe from Canadian Farm Cook Book.

preparation.description: Mix the butter to a cream, then add sugar, etc.
Roll thin, cut in cakes.

title: Strawberry Compote
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Picayune's Creole Cook Book.

preparation.description: Select fine strawberries, but not too ripe.
Wash them in cold water, and drain through a sieve.
Boil the sugar, and add the berries, and let them boil up once very gently.
Put them into a dish, pour the Jelly over, and serve.

title: Sour Milk Griddle Cakes (Hapanmaito pannukakkuja)
summary: Public-domain recipe from Suomalais-amerikalainen keittokirja.

preparation.description: Prepare and bake in the same way as the preceding griddle cakes.

title: One Egg Cake
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book.

preparation.description: Cream the butter, add sugar gradually, and egg well beaten.
Mix and sift flour and baking powder, add alternately with milk to first mixture.
Bake thirty minutes in a shallow pan.
Spread with Chocolate Frosting.

title: Ontario Pudding
summary: Public-domain recipe from Canadian Farm Cook Book.

preparation.description: Steam 1 hour

title: Strawberry Jam
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Picayune's Creole Cook Book.

preparation.description: Select fine, ripe strawberries and weigh.
Allow equal weights of fruit and sugar.
Proceed to boil as directed.
When they begin to jelly, they are ready to be turned into the jelly glasses.

title: Strawberry Cake
summary: Public-domain recipe from Suomalais-amerikalainen keittokirja.

preparation.description: Mash 1 quart of strawberries
Beat 5 yolks of eggs with sugar
mix with the mashed strawberries
Add 1 cupful of bread crumbs
At the last mix with the beaten whites of eggs
Bake in an individual mold
Serve cold with cream

title: One Egg Muffins I
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book.

preparation.description: Mix and sift dry ingredients; add gradually milk, egg well beaten, and melted butter.

title: White Fondant
summary: Public-domain recipe from The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book.

preparation.description: Put ingredients into a smooth granite stewpan.
Stir, place on range, and heat gradually to boiling-point.
Boil without stirring until, when tried in cold water, a soft ball may be formed that will just keep in shape, which is 238° F.
After a few minutes' boiling, sugar will adhere to sides of kettle; this should be washed off with the hand first dipped in cold water.

Have a pan of cold water near at hand, dip hand in cold water, then quickly wash off a small part of the sugar with tips of fingers, and repeat until all sugar adhering to side of saucepan is removed.
If this is quickly done, there is no danger of burning the fingers.
Pour slowly on a slightly oiled marble slab.
Let stand a few minutes to cool, but not long enough to become hard around the edge.
Scrape fondant with chopping knife to one end of marble, and work with a wooden spatula until white and creamy.
It will quickly change from this consistency, and begin to lump, when it should be kneaded with the hands until perfectly smooth.
Put into a bowl, cover with oiled paper to exclude air.
